title: add transactional downgrade-guard, backup/restore verification, and version-pinning for private-installer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need deterministic upgrade and rollback guarantees. This PR introduces a transactional downgrade guard for schema migrations, version-pinning for installer components, and end-to-end backup/restore verification hooks to avoid data loss during rollbacks. Scope: - Add transactional migration wrapper for Postgres schema changes (ensure either full apply or automatic rollback on failure) - Introduce a downgrade_guard controller that prevents downgrades when active migrations or incompatible data exists - Pin component images/helm chart versions in the installer manifest and add validation for mixed-version clusters - Add backup/restore verification step to the installer that validates logical backups and run a quick checksum verification post-restore - Expose a new CLI: redwood-installer verify-backup --snapshot <id> for operators - Update terraform module to expose a rollback_protection flag and support pre-upgrade snapshot TTL - Add unit and integration tests + e2e scenario for a simulated failed upgrade and automatic safe-rollback path

Checklist:
- [x] Transactional migration wrapper implemented and tested
- [x] Downgrade guard added and gated behind a feature flag (enabled by default for enterprise installs)
- [x] Version pinning and manifest validation added
- [x] Backup/restore verification CLI and installer hook implemented
- [x] Terraform module support and documented inputs
- [x] Added e2e test scenario and CI jobs

Notes: This is targeted at the private-installer workflow used by on-prem customers and VPC deployments. The changes are opt-out via feature flag for existing clusters but enabled by default for new installs. Related: ENG-4218 (upgrade safety), ENG-4250 (installer rollback UX), SUP-1573 (customer incident that motivated backup verification).

release_notes:
- Added transactional schema migration runner that ensures migrations are applied atomically and roll back on failure.
- Downgrade guard prevents unsafe downgrades when incompatible schema/data present; feature-flagged.
- Installer manifests now include explicit version pinning with an allowlist override.
- New 'redwood-installer verify-backup' CLI to validate logical backups as part of upgrade/rollback workflows.
- Terraform module adds 'rollback_protection' input to control snapshot/rollback behavior.
additional_context: This change was driven by a customer incident (SUP-1573) where a mid-upgrade crash left a cluster in a partially migrated state. The transactional runner reuses the existing migration framework but adds a two-phase apply with safe-exit guarantees and health checks. The downgrade guard integrates with the rollout controller to enforce safe rollbacks and emit diagnostics for support. We coordinated with the SRE team to add metrics and an alerting runbook.
notes_for_backport: Backport: if backporting to older release branches, ensure the postgres extension versions and transactional runner helpers are present; otherwise enable the feature flag off by default. Also pin the helm chart values to the older image tags used in the target branch.
